scope: Psalm 145:13 nun-line selection and verse 17 repeated-colon rendering; published evidence, not fresh decipherment
original_line: נאמן אלוהים בדבריו וחסיד בכול מעשיו
target: WLC-base critical composite with an isolated actual 11Q5 couplet, not the complete liturgical scroll Psalm
decision: Modest provisional inclusion preference; choose one attested Hebrew form instead of a harmonized retroversion. Exact earliest wording remains unresolved.
support: The missing acrostic position plus direct early Hebrew attestation and a corresponding Greek line without the scroll's recurrent blessing distinguish this unit from that particular refrain expansion. Their transmission relationship remains unestablished, so they are not mechanically counted as independent votes.
counterargument: An early editor could repair the missing alphabetic slot by composing a nun opening and reusing verse 17's second colon. Recurring blessings attest a different Psalm form; omission is also ancient. No original exemplar, copying event, intentional omission or direction of reuse is demonstrated.
chronology_sensitivity: Chronology modestly favors early attested inclusion, not necessarily earliest origin. Removing the age preference reduces the case to a structural/attestation preference and leaves repair versus loss unresolved.
known_hold_reassessment: Earlier pilot held exact-wording promotion while tentatively favoring inclusion. This pass separates provisional selection of an actual witness from proving earliest wording. It does not resolve God/LORD/all by fiat or claim new manuscript evidence. Source/English review and application gates remain required.
